name: fix_csharp_redos_nested_quantifier
description: Catastrophic-backtracking regex (nested quantifier) -> a linear pattern; budget calibrated in-container (vulnerable ~2.6s on a 26-char near-miss vs 0ms fixed, budget 500ms); incomplete-fix broken adds a MatchTimeout band-aid but keeps the vulnerable pattern, still tying up the caller for close to the full timeout
prompts: EmailValidator.IsValid(email) in EmailValidator.cs uses the pattern ^([a-zA-Z0-9]+)+@[a-zA-Z]+\.[a-zA-Z]+$ - the nested quantifier ([a-zA-Z0-9]+)+ has exponentially many ways to partition a run of matching characters, so a hostile near-miss input (many valid characters followed by one that breaks the match) triggers catastrophic backtracking and can hang the thread for seconds. Fix the REGEX itself: rewrite the pattern with no nested quantifier (a single [a-zA-Z0-9]+ for the local part is enough - it doesn't need to be wrapped in an outer +). Do not just bolt a MatchTimeout onto the existing vulnerable pattern as the fix - that still ties up the caller for close to the full timeout window on every hostile request, which is still a denial-of-service at scale. Valid addresses like user@example.com must still validate true.
